sampling_model.design: Known independent Bernoulli assignment with probability \(1/2\); assignment is the only sampling randomness.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population on \(r\) disjoint copies of a fixed known motif \(H\) with minimum degree two.
sampling_model.treatment: Each \(Z_{ka}\) is independent, and exposure is \(T_{ka}(Z)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every motif assignment has positive probability \(2^{-h}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. Baselines and direct effects are fixed adversarial nuisances; converse priors mix deterministic schedules only as a proof device.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: ArXiv version 2 Section 4 and Appendix B construct the Bernoulli quadratic-weight statistic; Proposition 4.1 states its \(d_{\max}^5/n\) MSE envelope using the variance ingredients in Lemmas S3--S4.
Theorem 2 establishes asymptotic validity for an estimated-residual randomization test while leaving theoretical power open.
Section 5 gives the Riesz representer and unbiased estimator and notes possible gains from alternative weights.
Proposition 3 gives a design-based Le Cam lower bound for squared-error estimation.
Theorems 1 and 2 match quadratic tests and mixture lower bounds in random-design regression.
Proposition 1 and Section 5 obtain exact nonsharp-null tests through focal artificial experiments.
Theorems 1 and 2 give valid conditional tests when the focal statistic is imputable.
The paper gives conditional tests for hierarchical interference specifications.

body.tldr: Using the Bernoulli-half moment-reproduction identities and quadratic weight imported from GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 Section 4 and Appendix B, this project studies a fixed network motif repeated under Bernoulli assignment. A \(2^h\)-row assignment table yields an exact robust semialgebraic program for the attained worst-schedule assignment-conditional variance and its least-favourable-prior dual. For a LinkedIn-style Bernoulli network experiment with a known repeated local motif, the contact-set certificate selects among feasible exposure-quadratic weights by the smallest worst bounded-schedule conditional-variance constant, thereby fixing the test threshold and power calibration relative to the published Gao et al. weight. The same table gives the explicit affinity factor \(L_H\), with certified comparisons for the nonisomorphic motifs \(K_3\) and \(C_4\). The optimal quadratic statistic is calibrated at finite-sample level over every bounded no-spillover schedule, and its fourth-root RMS signal scale is unavoidable for every measurable test. On degree-two motifs the feasible weight equals Gao et al.'s published weight, so the new content is the attained motif constant, exact calibration, and matching testing necessity rather than a strict improvement of the weight. Whether the quadratic test also attains the exact local power constant remains open.

project_justification.gap: GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 arXiv version 2 Section 4 and Appendix B supply the Bernoulli quadratic-weight construction, while Proposition 4.1 gives a \(d_{\max}^5/n\) MSE envelope from Lemmas S3--S4; available randomization tests provide validity without a theoretical local-power frontier.
project_justification.niche: Repeated fixed motifs isolate graph geometry from growing-degree asymptotics while preserving the practical Bernoulli design.
project_justification.fill: The project computes the attained variance saddle from a \(2^h\)-row robust semialgebraic program, uses its contact set to select the feasible exposure-quadratic weight with the smallest worst bounded-schedule conditional-variance constant for a known repeated motif, derives exact worst-null calibration by finite assignment and sign-pattern enumeration, and proves a matching all-test fourth-root lower bound with an explicit motif-computable Hellinger constant and certified \(K_3\) and \(C_4\) comparisons.

body.related_work: The Bernoulli-half moment-reproduction identities and quadratic weight are imported as background from GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 arXiv version 2 Section 4 and Appendix B. Its Proposition 4.1 gives a \(d_{\max}^5/n\) MSE envelope using the variance ingredients in Lemmas S3--S4. This paper is an informed-by comparator: on degree-two motifs the feasible weight is exactly Gao et al.'s weight, while the new repeated-motif results identify its attained worst-schedule conditional-variance constant, provide exact composite-null calibration, and prove the same fourth-root scale necessary for all tests. TiwariBasu2026 establishes validity for a different residual test but leaves theoretical local-power analysis unresolved. HarshawSavjeWang2022 informs the finite-dimensional Riesz geometry. KandirosHarshawSavje2026 informs the design-based Le Cam reduction. CommingesDalalyan2013 informs fourth-root quadratic testing. AtheyEcklesImbens2018, BasseFellerToulis2019, and HoshinoYanagi2026 provide focal-conditioning benchmarks without being theorem-level targets. Ni2026 surveys the design--power tension. PougetAbadieEtAl2019 supplies the LinkedIn-style Bernoulli network deployment: given the known repeated local motif, Theorem 1 selects among feasible exposure-quadratic weights by worst bounded-schedule conditional variance, which determines the exact test threshold and power calibration relative to the fixed GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 weight.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The explicit hard-prior calculation proves a constant-factor converse. The bound \(H^2(P_{0,a},P_{1,a})\le C_{\cos}r\xi_Ha^4\) does not identify the exact local likelihood experiment or establish quadratic sufficiency. The exact local power function and quadratic completeness remain in Open-ended Question 7.
body.honest_scope: The claims to prove are coercivity of the worst-schedule variance functional, variance-game attainment and duality, exact finite-sample control through explicit enumeration, the explicit fourth-order affinity lemma, a constant-factor all-test frontier, and exact motif certificates. The Bernoulli-half moment-reproduction identities, Gao et al.'s squared-separation convention, and their quadratic weight are imported background from GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 Section 4 and Appendix B and are not solve targets. On degree-two motifs the feasible weight equals the published weight, so no strict weight improvement is claimed. The exact local power curve and any nonquadratic advantage remain open. Exact elimination of the eight- and sixteen-row programs supplies the stated \(K_3\) and \(C_4\) values; the decimals report algebraic certificates rather than simulation output.
